We introduce the Russian Corpus of Linguistic Acceptability (RuCoLA)... The out-of-domain sentences are produced by nine open-source MT and paraphrase generation models... The out-of-domain set... to foster text generation evaluation with acceptability.
The motivation behind the out-of-domain set is to facilitate the practical use of acceptability judgments for improving language generation.
outputs: Generated sentences used as out-of-domain data in RuCoLA.
Machine‑translated and paraphrased Russian sentences generated by the listed models, which are later judged for linguistic acceptability.
The paper uses machine translation and paraphrase generation models to produce out-of-domain sentences for the RuCoLA benchmark, which are then evaluated for acceptability.

The out-of-domain sentences undergo a two-stage annotation procedure on Toloka, a crowdsourcing platform for data labeling... We collect the majority vote labels via a dynamic overlap from three to five workers after filtering them by response time and performance on control tasks.

We conduct a human evaluation on the entire in‑domain test set and 50% of the out‑of‑domain test set... The pay rate is on average $6.3/hr, and the task design is similar to Stage 1... annotators are undergraduate BA and MA students in philology and linguistics.

We conduct a human evaluation on the entire in-domain test set and 50% of the out-of-domain test set. The pay rate is on average $6.3/hr, and the task design is similar to Stage 1 in §3.3 (see also Table , Appendix B.1) with a few exceptions.
guideline: Workers judge whether a given sentence is acceptable or not; instructions include explanations of labels and examples.
Annotators label each sentence as acceptable or unacceptable (binary acceptability judgment).

The annotators are given detailed instructions describing the task, explaining the labels, and showing plenty of examples. The instruction is available at any time during both the training and main annotation phases.
